newsitem.title: BERMUDA: Tyco International has higher quarter, year.
newsitem.headline: Tyco International has higher quarter, year.

text.p: Tyco International Ltd., the world's largest manufacturer and installer of fire and safety systems, Monday reported higher fourth-quarter and full-year results.
The company said its earnings for the fourth quarter ended June 30 increased 46 percent to $137.9 million, or 82 cents per share, compared with last year's $94.2 million, or 62 cents per share.
Sales for the quarter increased 35 percent to $1.9 billion from last year's $1.4 billion.

"The internal growth of our existing companies was also enhanced by continued worldwide expansion of our products and services coupled with productivity enhancements which improved profit margins. All of this combines to provide a positive outlook for continued strong sales and earnings increases in our new fiscal year," said L. Dennis Kozlowski, Tyco's chairman.
For the fiscal year, earnings rose to $419.0 million, or $2.61 per share, a 35 percent increase over the $310.1 million, or $2.03 per share, reported last year.
Sales for the 1997 fiscal year reached $6.6 billion vs. $5.1 billion.

"We expect to see even further benefits as the acquisitions of ADT and Submarine Systems begin to contribute additional earnings as a result of their integration into Tyco's Fire and Safety Services and Electrical and Electronic Components units, respectively," Kozlowski said.

"We also look forward to the next several months when we expect to complete the acquisitions of Keystone International, which will become part of our Flow Control unit, and INBRAND Corp., which will combine with our Kendall healthcare operation," he said.

Tyco, based in Bermuda, also provides electronic security services, disposable medical products, packaging materials, flow control products, electrical and electronic components and underwater telecommunication cable systems.
Tyco's stock gained 75 cents to $77.6875 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
